details.question: What concept does the Progressive Disclosure paper propose?

Progressive Disclosure for an LLM-maintained wiki (arXiv 2607.04576) proposes layered disclosure: index, then summary, then the page, then the source quote.

lightrag.reason: LightRAG was not executed. Set ONTOWIKI_LIGHTRAG=1 only when an LLM endpoint and a built LightRAG index are available. No score is invented in their place.

notes.answer_hit: 1 when the gold answer string appears in the system answer, case-insensitive.
notes.context_tokens: Estimated tokens (characters/4) in the context the system returned for that question.
notes.lightrag: Left not-run. LightRAG needs an LLM endpoint; this harness does not fabricate that run.
notes.ontowiki: Answer comes from ontology-checked claims filtered by transaction time (as_of). Context is the progressive-disclosure bundle: index, answer, valid time, quote.
notes.source_recall: Fraction of gold source filenames among the sources the system used. OntoWiki cites the episodes of the claims it answered from. Vector RAG cites its top-3 chunks.
notes.traceable: 1 when the source that produced the answer is one of the gold sources.
notes.vector_rag: TF-IDF over source prose. The ontology block is stripped before indexing. The answer is the best-overlapping sentence in the top chunk. as_of is ignored.
